# glinet_multiwan_interface (Resource)

Manages the tracking of a multi-WAN interface of the router (`kmwan.set_interface` in the router API). The router finds out whether an interface is online: it sends requests to the track hosts of the interface.

~> **Warning:** a write can change the uplink that the router uses, and so can cut the Internet access of the router and of its clients.

When the track hosts do not answer, the router thinks that the interface is offline and can stop using it. Use one instance of this resource for each interface. The interface always exists on the router, so create takes over the interface. Each attribute that is not set keeps the value of the router: the provider sends back the value that it reads from the router just before the write. The provider writes only when a value differs from the router, so a create whose values are equal to those of the router sends no write. It sends the fields as the web UI does: always `interface` and `enable_check`; when `check_enabled` is `true`, also `track_proto`, `track_method` and `track_mode`, `track_ipv4` when `track_protocol` is `ipv4` or `both`, and `track_ipv6` when `track_protocol` is `ipv6` or `both`. It sends back the `track_method` of the router (the web UI lists only ping, `0`) and, for `track_method` `1`, the `enable_ssl` of the router. It is not known whether the router keeps the fields that a write does not send. The failover order and the weights are in `glinet_multiwan`. The write of this resource was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glinet_multiwan_interface" "wan" {
  interface      = "wan"
  check_enabled  = true
  track_mode     = "normal"
  track_protocol = "ipv4"
  track_ipv4     = ["192.0.2.1", "198.51.100.1"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `interface` (String) Name of the interface on the router, for example `wan`, `secondwan`, `wwan` (repeater) or `tethering` (`interface` in the router API). Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `check_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the router tracks the interface with the track hosts (`enable_check` in the router API). When it is `false`, the router uses only the physical state of the interface, and the other attributes cannot be set. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `track_ipv4` (List of String) Two to four IPv4 addresses of the track hosts (`track_ipv4` in the router API), as the web UI requires. The router uses them when `track_protocol` is `ipv4` or `both`; they cannot be set when it is `ipv6`. Create and update fail without a write when the router would get fewer than two hosts for a protocol that it tracks. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `track_ipv6` (List of String) Two to four IPv6 addresses of the track hosts (`track_ipv6` in the router API), as the web UI requires. The router uses them when `track_protocol` is `ipv6` or `both`; they cannot be set when it is `ipv4`. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `track_mode` (String) Track mode: `normal`, `low_data` (badge "passive" in the web UI) or `strict` (`track_mode` `1`, `0` or `2` in the router API). How the modes differ is not known. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `track_protocol` (String) IP version of the tracking: `ipv4`, `ipv6` or `both` (`track_proto` `0`, `1` or `2` in the router API). The web UI lets the user select it only when IPv6 is enabled on the router; the provider does not check this. When it is not set, the router value does not change.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the name of the multi-WAN interface on the router.
terraform import glinet_multiwan_interface.wan wan
```
